Isoleucine degradation disorder, usually asymptomatic; neurologic findings occur in 5-29%, and muscle findings from one patient do not establish common involvement.
Congenital ventricular septal defect; additional reported abnormalities are also cardiovascular.

Immune-mediated epidermal necrosis; destructive oral mucositis occurs in about 90%. Lasting ocular injury and other organ complications are below 30%.
Yersinia enterocolitica primarily causes intestinal infection and enterocolitis; systemic complications are uncommon.
Congenital structural defect of the ulna with abnormal bone continuity.
Inherited nephropathy with defining abnormal urate handling and hyperuricemia; gout is a separately diagnosed joint disease.
Inflammation of the olecranon bursa; infection or autoimmune disease is not intrinsic to this umbrella diagnosis.

Autophagic skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency and extraocular movement limitation occur in only 5-29%.
Tuberculous infection directly involves ocular tissues; pulmonary disease is not inherent to this extrapulmonary diagnosis.
Alpha-globin deficiency causes hemolytic anemia; splenic involvement remains hematologic. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Inherited immunodeficiency with abnormal lymphocyte proliferation; lymphoma and hemophagocytic syndromes are separate diagnoses, not additional organ labels.
Obstetric ectopic implantation; abdominal location alone does not establish damage to a particular covered organ.
Keratin-filled cyst arising from the hair follicle outer root sheath, usually in scalp skin.
Defined by impaired development of cognitive, motor or social nervous-system functions; additional organs are subtype-specific.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; accommodation impairment is frequent (30-79%) and structural microtia occurs in 80-99%. Arachnodactyly alone does not establish locomotor damage.
